newsitem.title: CHINA: China cuts number of urban poor by 660,000 in '96.
newsitem.headline: China cuts number of urban poor by 660,000 in '96.

text.p: Many of China's urban poor grew poorer last year but more than 660,000 urban Chinese were lifted out of poverty, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
China's urban poor totalled 11.76 million at the end of 1996, it said.

The achievement in bringing 660,000 people out of poverty was a result of projects to help the poor through re-employment or by establishing minimum living standards for urban residents, Xinhua said, quoting the State Statistical Bureau.
In 1996, 84 percent of China's urban poor were those who had lost their jobs as a result of China's market-oriented economic reforms, it said.

About 40 percent of these were former workers in state-owned or collective firms, especially in the coal, machinery, and textile sectors, which have been particularly hard hit by reforms to force lumbering government firms to sink or swim in a market economy.
The report said 85 percent of the urban poor lived in economically backward regions in central and western China.
The standard of living of China's urban poor was deteriorating, the bureau said.
In 1996, their annual per capita income dropped 12 percent to 1,321 yuan ($160), equivalent to 30 percent of the average per capita income of urban residents.
China set a poverty line for urban residents at 1,700 yuan per capita and to help the poor to live above the poverty line, China's needs 4.2 billion yuan in relief funds this year, it said.
Some 65 million Chinese nationwide live in poverty and the vast majority are rural poor.
